note: Staying in tune through a whole tune: with the chords, then the tune muted over the chords, then the tune alone and a cappella, then a verse of a song the singer knows over a drone. The old Key choice of the last block is moves (key any), and the line about another key opens with {{?key}}. Missing: a song tool (a whole song's melody and words to sing through with the mic; the longest tunes in the melody book are 4 bars).

exercise.title: A whole song in tune
exercise.why: Pitch drifts a little on every long note and every breath, and over a whole song the drift adds up, so check the long notes against something that holds the key: the chords, then your own ear, then a drone.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune over its chords: the mic starts with it. Sing along on "ah", and watch your line on the two long notes in the second bar: {{5}}, then the {{5}} an octave under it.
Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
If your line sags on a long note, sing that note again more quietly.

Press Play below to hear the same tune with nothing under it: the mic starts with it. Sing along once on "ah".
Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it a cappella.
Practice until your last {{1}} is the {{1}} the tune started on.

Pick a song in a major key that you know by heart. Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together.
Sing a whole verse with its words, with the drone as the song's {{1}}, and watch where your line sits on the long notes.
When a phrase has drifted, its last note no longer blends with the drone: sing that phrase again before you go on.
{{?key}}In another key the drone sits higher or lower, and it is still the song's {{1}}.
